subject: Plot of uncertainty (dsm), R, raster package

messages.author: fa112d5a5313e536
messages.subject: Plot of uncertainty (dsm), R, raster package
parts:
Dear All,

Trying to produce a grid layer output (raster package) of uncertainty over a prediction grid. Based on the dsm manual I have done the following:

pred.new <- split(prd.rst.df,1:nrow(prd.rst.df))
# prd.rst.df > data frame with covariates, x,y and off.set columns
#results in a very large list (30,000 elements), including off.set as one column
dsm.pred.var <- dsm.var.gam(dsm.mod, pred.new, prd.rst.df$off.set,
                            seglen.varname = "Effort", type.pred = "response")

I expecting that this function would add "pred.var" column to each list element, which I then could ultimately "cbind" with a rasterFromXYZ function. However, running the above sequence causes my laptop to freeze, so I am wondering if 1) code is incorrect or 2) may be too many list elements?

I have not found any examples online for creating a raster grid of the CV's - only using ggplot based vector plots.

Many thanks for any pointers or help in advance!

Don

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Plot of uncertainty (dsm), R, raster package
parts:
Hi Don, hi listfolk,

The code looks correct to me. Likely the issue is that the data is too
big. You can reduce the memory load by removing any columns you don't
need from prd.rst.df prior to splitting.

I think it's fine in this situation to "chunk up" the prediction grid
and do variance estimation on subsets of prd.rst.df. Template code
(UNTESTED!) below. Hope this helps.


cheers,
--dave

---

# create block indexes of 1000 entries (could increase this)
chunk_start <- c(seq(1, nrow(prd.rst.df)+1, by=1000))
chunk_end <- c(chunk_start[2:length(chunk_start)]-1, nrow(prd.rst.df))

# storage
vars <- rep(NA, nrow(prd.rst.df))

# loop over the index
for(ii in seq_along(chunk_start)){

# get the current chunk
this_chunk <- prd.rst.df[chunk_start[ii]:chunk_end[ii], ]
# split
pred.new <- split(this_chunk, 1:nrow(this_chunk))
# estimate variance
dsm.pred.var <- dsm.var.gam(dsm.mod, pred.new, this_chunk$off.set,

# extract the cell variances
vars[chunk_start[ii]:chunk_end[ii]] <- dsm.pred.var$pred.var

}
